chunks: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Sayābah asked him:
About fish that are caught, then placed in something, then returned to the water and die in it, he said: “Do not eat it, because it died in that wherein its life is.”

key_terms.السَّمَكِ: fish, the animal being asked about in the ruling
key_terms.الْمَاءِ: water, the environment to which the fish was returned
key_terms.حَيَاتُهُ: its life, meaning the medium in which it normally lives

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat a fish that was caught and then died after being returned to the water?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning fish that are caught alive and then returned to water, where they die. The Imam عليه السلام forbids eating such fish because its death occurred in water, which is the environment of its life, making it impermissible in this context.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4154 - Abd al-Rahman ibn Sayabah asked him

about fish that are caught, placed in something, and then returned to the water where they die.
Imam (as) said: "Do not eat it, because it died in what is its source of life."
